chapter: Maple Leaf, own orchestra and rivals
title: Learning your audience; King Oliver in the Irish Channel
summary: Charles says his smooth style failed with rough Italian crowds who wanted Oliver's growling mute work.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: What about the tempo of tunes? How fast would be the fastest one you'd play?
Well it's all the band. It all depends?

Yeah, it's all depends on who you was playing with, for, too. That's another band. You see, that's like anything else. You've got to learn your people. See? Some of the people who had to play some rough stuff there, I mean rough, very rough. And some people, if you didn't play nice music, you didn't play nothing. Because let me show you what happened. I came here for a vacation. And I put Joe Olive on my place. You all heard about King Olive. And he was playing, that day I was playing with the Silver Leaf band. You see, those people that you see on it. And all on the front there, around the Irish Channel, they couldn't see nobody else but Olive. And over and around, you know, in Country Club, and many other places, they all knew where I was at. You see? And when I went back, they wanted to know where was King, where was Olive, because they didn't like my playing. Is that right?
So you see, you've got to learn your people. You sure do.

Because now you take the dang tag on Chapitula Street all around the Irish Channel there. That's a rough Italian part. That's right. And they wanted that rough stuff, you see? But I couldn't play it like they wanted it, you see?
But King Oliver could. So Oliver could bend notes and make his trumpet talk with the mute and everything.

You see, old King Oliver, he'd take one number there, you'd be playing that whole number almost, and he'd be just right there. Peep, peepireep, peepireep, peepireep, peepireep, peepireep, peepireep, peepireep, peepireep, you see? That's all he'd be doing. And they liked that. But I couldn't see that.
It surely wasn't smooth. You see?

I couldn't see that. It was rough. But they liked it. It's somewhat the better, you see? Yes, that's an Irish Channel for you, you see? That's why I said it's just the people. You've got to learn your people and give them satisfaction. Of course we played for them, but at the same time they were asking where was that trumpet playing. And come right before the band there too and ask why that fellow with the funny eye. They were. That was Joe on him. He got hit in the eye.
